challenge.title: Autonomy and Community Response Evidence Challenge
challenge.description: Complete 10 activities: six clue-and-conclusion decisions and four matching tasks. Both parts of an evidence decision count together as one activity. Get at least 7 activities correct. All supplied lesson clues are available without saving them in your journal.

badge.name: Autonomy and Community Response Investigator
badge.description: Earned by completing four Chapter 11 missions and passing the evidence challenge. Recognizes careful explanations of claims, actual authority, distinct communities and varied responses.

evidence.question: A colonial map claim is treated as proof that authority was carried out everywhere. Which clue directly identifies the evidence needed?
choices: Effective control needs evidence of authority actually carried out
A map color proves every order was obeyed
One visit guarantees permanent control
A claim reveals every local decision
evidence.explanation: Separate an asserted claim from evidence of authority in practice in a particular place and period.

evidence.question: One military post is used to claim identical authority throughout surrounding communities. Which clue directly checks this extension?
choices: A post in one place does not establish the same authority everywhere around it
One post proves every local decision followed colonial orders
Every community had one identical experience
No further evidence is needed outside the post
evidence.explanation: Keep a posts location distinct from wider claims about control. Investigate actual local authority.

evidence.question: A report treats Sulu and Maguindanao as two names for one government. Which clue directly checks that claim?
choices: They were separate polities with connections
They were identical in every period
One religion means one government everywhere
A modern province supplies every historical boundary
evidence.explanation: Identify each polity and its setting. Connections do not make distinct institutions identical.

evidence.question: A date from one deposit is used to date every terrace in the Cordillera. Which clue directly checks the scope?
choices: A deposit or one site does not establish one date for every terrace
One find gives every landscape the same age
Looking traditional establishes a universal date
A region has one unchanged history
evidence.explanation: Match a date to its recorded context and supported feature rather than extend it to the whole region.

evidence.question: A report says every form of resistance was armed fighting. Which clue directly checks the definition?
choices: Not every form of resistance is armed fighting
Every change was a battle
Every absence proves deliberate opposition
The strongest response is always the one causing harm
evidence.explanation: Investigate particular actions opposing a demand. Support the connection with evidence and do not reward harm.

evidence.question: A response is called successful only because its aim was recorded. Which clue directly checks the claim?
choices: What people sought and what followed are different claims
Every aim guarantees its outcome
Every result is permanent
One leaders aim proves every household benefited
evidence.explanation: Seek evidence about what followed, for whom and when. State uncertainty when outcome evidence is missing.

matching.question: Match these authority questions with the evidence to seek.
pairs: What authority was actually carried out
matching.explanation: Claims, practice and local decisions need distinct evidence. Contact is not automatic conquest, and autonomy is not isolation.

matching.question: Match these polity and source ideas with their meanings.
pairs: A polity headed by a sultan
Managing relationships through communication and negotiation
Evidence of how written commitments worked in practice
matching.explanation: Keep distinct polities, text versions and actual outcomes visible. A ruler or religion does not describe every community members experience.

matching.question: Match these Cordillera investigation ideas with their careful descriptions.
pairs: A particular group and setting within a wider region
Where evidence was found and its relationships
Researchers and descendant communities contributing to interpretation
matching.explanation: A regional label is not one identical population. A context date or modern collection is not every earlier feature or practice.

matching.question: Match each response idea with its meaning.
pairs: Adjusting activities or arrangements to conditions
What followed an action, supported by evidence
matching.explanation: Adaptation and resistance can coexist. People could act within limits, and aims are not proof of outcomes.
